2.31	How many electrons in an atom may have the following quantum numbers?
	(a)  n = 4, ms = – ½			(b)  n = 3, l = 0
2.32	Show that the circumference of the Bohr orbit for the hydrogen atom is an integral multiple of the de Broglie wavelength associated with the electron revolving around the orbit.
2.33	What transition in the hydrogen spectrum would have the same wavelength as the Balmer transition n = 4 to n = 2 of  He+ spectrum ?

2.34	Calculate the energy required for the process
	He+ (g)  He2+ (g) + e–
	The ionization energy for the H atom in the ground state is 2.18 × 10–18 J atom–1
2.35	If the diameter of a carbon atom is 0.15 nm, calculate the number of carbon atoms which can be placed side by side in a straight line across length of scale of length 20 cm long.
2.36	2 ×108 atoms of carbon are arranged side by side. Calculate the radius of carbon atom if the length of this arrangement is 2.4 cm.
2.37	The diameter of zinc atom is 2.6 Å. Calculate (a) radius of zinc atom in pm and (b) number of atoms present in a length of 1.6 cm if the zinc atoms are arranged side by side lengthwise.
2.38	A certain particle carries 2.5 × 10–16C of static electric charge. Calculate the number of electrons present in it.

2.39	In Milikan’s experiment, static electric charge on the oil drops has been obtained by shining X-rays. If the static electric charge on the oil drop is –1.282 × 10–18C, calculate the number of electrons present on it.

2.40	In Rutherford’s experiment, generally the thin foil of heavy atoms, like gold, platinum etc. have been used to be bombarded by the α-particles. If the thin foil of light atoms like aluminium etc. is used, what difference would be observed from the above results ?
2.42	An element with mass number 81 contains 31.7% more neutrons as compared to protons. Assign the atomic symbol.
2.43	An ion with mass number 37 possesses one unit of negative charge. If the ion conatins 11.1% more neutrons than the electrons, find the symbol of the ion.
2.44	An ion with mass number 56 contains 3 units of positive charge and 30.4% more neutrons than electrons. Assign the symbol to this ion.

2.45	Arrange the following type of radiations in increasing order of frequency: (a) radiation from microwave oven (b) amber light from traffic signal (c) radiation from FM radio (d) cosmic rays from outer space and (e) X-rays.
2.46	Nitrogen laser produces a radiation at a wavelength of 337.1 nm. If the number of photons emitted is 5.6 × 1024, calculate the power of this laser.

2.47	Neon gas is generally used in the sign boards. If it emits strongly at 616 nm, calculate (a) the frequency of emission, (b) distance traveled by this radiation in 30 s  (c) energy of quantum and (d) number of quanta present if it produces 2 J of energy.

note: Seam judged against CHE11L-ch02-p042.runA.json, written immediately before this page (the instruction's named anchor p030 has no output on disk). p042's exercise 2.30 is cut off after answer row (d) and its last_block_continues_on_next is true; this page opens with rows (e) and (f) of that same 2.30 set — printed with no item number of their own, just ' (e)  n = 3, l = 3, ml = –3, ms = + ½' and ' (f)  n = 3, l = 1, ml = 0, ms = + ½' — before 2.31 begins, so block n=1 is the tail of 2.30 and first_block_continues_from_previous is true. The two pages agree. input's previous_page_last_block was null. last_block_continues_on_next is false: 2.47 ends on the complete word 'energy.', the bottom fifth of the page is blank, and p043's successor opens with a fresh item, 2.48 ('In astronomical observations, signals observed from the distant stars ...'), so p044 must set first_block_continues_from_previous false. The page is the single-column continuation of the EXERCISES section, items 2.30(e)-(f) and 2.31 to 2.47, one list block per numbered exercise with its lettered sub-parts inside it, in the printed order the text layer also uses. Block n=12 is the ONLY deferral and it is exercise 2.41, deferred WHOLE with a bbox over both of its printed lines. This is the one place on the page where the layer is scrambled beyond faithful transcription rather than merely flattened: the item is printed 'Symbols [79 over 35]Br and [79]Br can be written, whereas symbols [35 over 79]Br and [35]Br are not acceptable. Answer briefly.', and the text layer stores it with the mass and atomic numbers HOISTED AND REVERSED — verbatim 'Symbols 35' / '79Br and 79Br can be written, whereas symbols 79' / '35Br and 35Br are not' / 'acceptable. Answer briefly.' Following the layer's token order would assert the symbol as 35-then-79, i.e. the opposite of what the page prints, and reconstructing the printed superscripts would manufacture numbers (3579, 7935) that are nowhere in the layer; marking the region needs_special is the step's prescribed way out, so the four nuclide symbols and the prose around them go to the special transcriber together. Everywhere else the inline quantities follow the layer's own flattened spelling rather than the printed superscripts: 'of  He+ spectrum ?', 'He+ (g)  He2+ (g) + e–', '2.18 × 10–18 J atom–1' with no closing full stop as printed, '2 ×108 atoms of carbon' (the layer's flattening of 2 × 10-to-the-8, with its missing space), '2.5 × 10–16C' and '–1.282 × 10–18C' with no space before the C, and '5.6 × 1024' (its flattening of 5.6 × 10-to-the-24). One genuine gap recorded rather than papered over: in block n=5 the reaction arrow of 2.34 is ABSENT from the text layer, which stores the line as 'He+ (g)  He2+ (g) + e–' with a bare double space where the printed right arrow stands; following the earlier pages' precedent for the missing wavenumber symbol I have transcribed what the layer has rather than inventing the glyph, and the printed character there is a right arrow. 'conatins' in 2.43 and 'traveled' in 2.47 are as printed and not corrected; the doubled spaces ('of  He+ spectrum', 'in 30 s  (c) energy'), the alpha glyph in 'α-particles', the one-half glyphs and the tab indents are the layer's and the page's own. bboxes are original-image pixels (1750x2180); the image renders at 1606x2000, so displayed coordinates were scaled by 1.09.
